reasoning: The U.S. has not conducted a nuclear weapons test since 1992, when it conducted its last test at the Nevada Test Site. The U.S. is a signatory to the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty (CTBT), which it signed in 1996, though it has not ratified it. The timeframe is extremely short (March 6-31, 2026, only ~25 days). There is no credible indication of imminent U.S. nuclear testing. Such a test would represent a dramatic policy reversal with massive geopolitical consequences. While the CTBT remains unratified, actual testing would be unprecedented in the modern era and would require extraordinary circumstances. The probability of a U.S. nuclear test within this narrow window is extremely low.
